en: Rudolf Hess in the dock of the International Military Tribunal at Nuremberg as its judgment is read, beside the other defendants: Hermann Göring on one side, Joachim von Ribbentrop on the other. On 30 September 1946, the first of the judgment's two days, Hess shows distress, his head in his hand, rocking forward and back, until he stands and is led out of the dock. The film shows him back in the dock before the day's adjournment, and on 1 October, as the verdicts on the defendants are read, his own among them. Its annotations follow him, and the defendants around him, through the film.
Sentencing of Nazi Leaders at Nuremberg

MS, Hermann Goering, Baldur von Schirach, Joachim von Ribbentrop, Wilhelm Keitel, Alfred Jodl, Rudolf Hess, sitting in prisoners' dock listening to testimony. Hess taken ill leaves prisoners' dock. Shots of English and US prosecution tables. Scenes of Justice Kravechenko, Russian Justice, reading statement from bench. Pan of prisoners' dock and courtroom as voice of Justice Sir Geoffrey Lawrence (British) is heard speaking about the SS, Slave Labor and experiments on human beings. The SS was able to procure funds for human experiments from the government. The extermination of the Jews was carried out by the SS.. Court adjourns. MS of Erich Raeder, Fritz Sauckel, Hess, Goering, von Ribbentrop, in dock. Justice Francis Biddle in speaking of von Ribbentrop declares that the latter merely stated he acted as a rubber stamp for Adolf Hitler's ideas. The tribunal however, finds him guilty on all counts. Camera on prisoners' dock as Justice Lawrence speaks about the defendant, Ernst Kaltenbrunner.
